findings.note: internal/fsm/run/types.go:371 double-quotes the run id: fmt.Errorf("invalid run id %q", strconv.Quote(id)). strconv.Quote already returns a quoted, escaped literal and %q quotes and escapes it a second time, so an id containing a quote surfaces to the user as \"a\\\"b\" instead of "a\"b". ValidateRunID's error text reaches operators through internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:222-228 and internal/fsm/export/export.go:89, so this is user-visible. Use %s with strconv.Quote, or %q with the bare id.

findings.note: internal/fsm/run/store.go:154-163: on every Append, prepareAppend walks all previously stored lines and runs json.Unmarshal on each one via lineType (store.go:171-177) purely to recount counted events. With DefaultMaxEvents at 100_000 (types.go), this makes the counted-event check quadratic in run length on top of the store's existing full-file re-read. The count is derivable incrementally from FoldState, which the caller already carries across the CAS. Not urgent at realistic run lengths, but the cap it enforces is the one that makes long runs possible in the first place.

findings.note: internal/fsm/run/store.go:92-99: parseLines decodes exactly one JSON value per stored line and never calls dec.More(), so any bytes after the closing brace on a line are silently dropped, while LineHash(line) at store.go:105 hashes the whole line. The decoded Event can therefore diverge from the bytes the audit chain attests to, and the same read path accepts duplicate object keys that Canonical (internal/fsm/run/canonical.go:22) refuses on write - the write-side canonicality invariant is not re-checked on read. This is bounded (an actor who can rewrite the file can rewrite the chain too, since no head is anchored outside the file), but for a package whose stated job is a tamper-evident audit log it is a gap worth closing with a dec.More() check.

evidence.note: prevHash = LineHash(line) hashes bytes the decoder may have partly ignored.

findings.note: internal/fsm/gate/gate_test.go:170-183: repo() runs git init/commit in a t.TempDir with only author/committer identity pinned via env. The ambient global git config still applies, so a developer or CI image with commit.gpgsign=true, init.templateDir, or a core.hooksPath pointing at a hook that rejects commits will fail these tests for reasons unrelated to the code under test. The production seam is careful here (internal/fsm/gate/git.go:57 documents config-injection hardening, and scrubEnv strips GIT_* overrides), so the test helper is the weaker half. Passing -c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null (and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null) to the helper would make the fixture hermetic.

evidence.note: git init in a temp dir with ambient global config still in effect.

findings.note: tests/go/test-shardpack-coverage.sh:11 sends go test stdout to /dev/null, and go test writes test failures and panics to stdout, so the failure branch prints only 'shardpack coverage: go test failed' with every diagnostic discarded - the operator has to re-run the command by hand to learn anything. Capture the output to a variable or a temp file and echo it on the failure path. Relatedly, tests/run-all.sh:20 guards the invocation with 'if [ -f ... ]', so if this script is ever moved or deleted the 100%-coverage gate stops running silently rather than failing.
